/* HTIF syscall-window client: the uncached SimControl mailbox protocol
 * shared by every andesim runtime payload (vplat today; vlinux next). The
 * window lives in DEVICE space (PMA-uncached on every engine), so the
 * exchange is coherent by construction on any cache hierarchy, including a
 * private write-back L2 (ax66 PL2C) that a cacheable-RAM mailbox cannot
 * survive: the guest would read its own stale copy of the host's result,
 * and no guest-side CCTL sequence can fix that (the VA-scoped forms trap
 * on RVH cores, the ALL forms drop unrelated dirty lines).
 *
 *   stdio (fd 0-2)  ATCUART100 UART2: THR @0xf0300020, LSR @0xf0300034.
 *   file io (fd>2)  the SimControl syscall WINDOW @0xe0080800: eight u64
 *                   arg/result slots + a data area for payloads, doorbell
 *                   @0xe0080028. Served host-side (vsim: sim_control.hpp
 *                   dispatch_window; QEMU: andes_ae350.c's mirror).
 *
 * No semihosting, no ecall, and no "which engine am I on" probe -- hybrid
 * migrates the running process between engines, so any boot-time detection
 * would go stale at the handoff. Every call must be engine-blind.
 */

#include <stddef.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <sys/types.h>

/* HTIF syscall numbers -- must match the table in the vsim repo's
 * src/platform/sim_control.hpp (and the QEMU mirror device). */

#define VH_SYS_OPEN         6
#define VH_SYS_WRITE        7
#define VH_SYS_GETCWD       8
#define VH_SYS_LSEEK        9
#define VH_SYS_READ         10
#define VH_SYS_FLEN         11
#define VH_SYS_CLOSE        12
#define VH_SYS_ACCESS       13
#define VH_SYS_FACCESSAT    14
#define VH_SYS_FSTAT        15
#define VH_SYS_FSTATAT      16
#define VH_SYS_LINK         17
#define VH_SYS_LSTAT        18
#define VH_SYS_STAT         19
#define VH_SYS_OPENAT       20
#define VH_SYS_RENAME       21
#define VH_SYS_UNLINK       22

/* Window layout -- must match the hosts (vsim src/platform/sim_control.hpp
 * SYSCALL_WINDOW_*; QEMU hw/riscv/andes_ae350.c ANDESIM_SYSCALL_*). All
 * guest accesses are u64 loads/stores (the access width every engine
 * already proves out on the legacy 0x10 doorbell). */
#define WIN_DATA_VA 0xe0080840UL
#define WIN_DATA_SIZE (0x800u - 0x40u) /* 1984 bytes, 8-aligned */

/* Console output; blocks until UART2's transmit-holding register drains. */
void htif_uart_putc(char c);

/* One window syscall: stage the slots, ring the doorbell, read the result.
 * The doorbell write is an uncached device store, so the host has served
 * the call before the store retires; the fence orders the result load. */
intptr_t htif_syscall(uint64_t n, uint64_t a0, uint64_t a1, uint64_t a2,
                       uint64_t a3);

/* Raw copies into/out of the window data area (u64 accesses only). `woff`
 * is a byte offset into the data area and must be 8-aligned. */
void htif_win_store(size_t woff, const void* src, size_t len);
void htif_win_load(void* dst, size_t woff, size_t len);

/* Stage a string at data-area offset `woff`; returns the byte offset just
 * past its NUL, rounded up to 8, or (size_t)-1 if it does not fit. */
size_t htif_win_store_str(size_t woff, const char* s);

/* Marshaling helpers for the recurring one/two-string-argument shapes. */

/* fd>2 write/read, chunked through the window data area (WIN_DATA_SIZE
 * bytes per round trip); stops early on a short transfer, same contract as
 * a POSIX write()/read(). Callers own the fd<=2 (console) special case. */
ssize_t htif_write(int fd, const void* ptr, size_t len);

155	   the RISC-V branch was the only outlier, not a hardware requirement.

163	   quant kernel in the same file (which dispatch across
164	   vl1024/vl512/vl256/vl128 variants). `ax45mpv_premium`'s vector FPU

167	   immediately before the float op faults -- this is FP-datapath-specific,
168	   not a blanket LMUL cap; correlates with the engine's `isa-vl4` config

170	   this one surfaces on vsim rather than QEMU1, unlike fixes 1/2/4). Fix:
171	   both functions now call their existing portable `_ref` scalar
172	   implementations (`ggml/src/ggml-quants.c`, already used as the non-RVV

174	   quantization, called once per token row before the (still fully

176	   matmul cost.

179	   handler (shared by every andesim runtime, vplat and vlinux alike)
180	   calls `fprintf` then `_exit()`; `_exit()` never flushes stdio, so on a

186	   `fprintf` itself). This is what made fix 3 possible to diagnose in the
187	   first place -- see `ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md`'s U9 section for the full
188	   trail.

194	cmake -B build-rv64-static -UGGML_RV_ZVE32F \
195	  -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS="-mext-zvlsseg -DANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K=51 -I /path/to/andesim/build/runtime/include" \
196	  -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS="-mext-zvlsseg -DANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K=51 -I /path/to/andesim/build/runtime/include"

199	# in andesim:
200	./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --runtime linux --mem-size 2000M \
201	  --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium --step-timeout-ms 900000 \
202	  /path/to/llama.cpp/build-rv64-static/bin/llama-completion \
203	  -- -m /path/to/models/Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf -no-cnv \
204	     --prompt "The capital of France is" -n 32 -c 512 -t 1
205	```

5	(fast / cycle / hybrid) **unmodified**, with real argv, and hybrid

7	target: `llama-completion` (llama.cpp's text-generation CLI, `tools/completion/`

10	How: a small M-mode **proxy kernel** (`vlinux.elf`, new `runtime/linux/`
11	component, pattern: riscv-pk) that loads the app ELF, builds the Linux
12	initial stack (argc/argv/envp/auxv), and answers the app's `ecall`s by
13	emulating ~30 Linux syscalls on top of the existing HTIF syscall window.
14	The hybrid transport, triggers, plugin, resume driver, and engines need
15	NO changes: the guest stays bare-metal, M-mode, paging-off, single-hart,
16	exactly the current ROI envelope.

18	Non-goals (explicitly out of scope here)

20	  (that is FRS FR-109, a separate track).

22	  (verified: at n_threads=1 ggml never calls pthread_create, and
23	  uncontended glibc mutexes never reach futex).

27	  that lift is feature U10 (platform track). Until then use a
28	  layer-sliced GGUF (U11) - per-layer kernel shapes are identical.
29	  NOT on the critical path: the primary target Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf

65	## Guest memory map (vlinux contract, DRAM base 0x0)
66	
67	| Region                  | Range                          | Owner |
68	|-------------------------|--------------------------------|-------|
69	| ILM aperture            | 0x0000_0000 .. 0x0000_FFFF     | platform (apps link at >= 0x10000, no overlap) |
70	| App image (PT_LOADs)    | link base (0x10000/0x50000) .. | app ELF; loader rejects overlap with vlinux |

75	| V-scratch               | `mem_size` .. +4 KB            | hybrid V transport (existing, untouched) |

78	across it is transported by the existing LM sidecars (probe-verified).

# Linux-Runtime Roadmap: run static glibc binaries (llama.cpp) on andesim

Goal: a prebuilt RISC-V **static glibc** binary (built with the Andes
`nds64le-linux-glibc-v5d` toolchain) runs on every andesim mode
(fast / cycle / hybrid) **unmodified**, with real argv, and hybrid
measures ONE kernel iteration (marker or PC trigger) on vsim. Primary
target: `llama-completion` (llama.cpp's text-generation CLI, `tools/completion/`
in `/home/nick/work/llama.cpp`) generating text from `Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf`.

How: a small M-mode **proxy kernel** (`vlinux.elf`, new `runtime/linux/`
component, pattern: riscv-pk) that loads the app ELF, builds the Linux
initial stack (argc/argv/envp/auxv), and answers the app's `ecall`s by
emulating ~30 Linux syscalls on top of the existing HTIF syscall window.
The hybrid transport, triggers, plugin, resume driver, and engines need
NO changes: the guest stays bare-metal, M-mode, paging-off, single-hart,
exactly the current ROI envelope.

Non-goals (explicitly out of scope here)
- No real Linux kernel boot, no S/U-mode, no paging, no interrupts
  (that is FRS FR-109, a separate track).
- No threads: `clone` returns -ENOSYS; llama.cpp runs with `-t 1`
  (verified: at n_threads=1 ggml never calls pthread_create, and
  uncontended glibc mutexes never reach futex).
- No dynamic linking: the app must be `-static` (the toolchain ships
  `libc.a`; a static hello links at vaddr 0x50000, inside DRAM).
- Full 3.8 GB Bonsai-27B residency is blocked by the 2 GiB DRAM window;
  that lift is feature U10 (platform track). Until then use a
  layer-sliced GGUF (U11) - per-layer kernel shapes are identical.
  NOT on the critical path: the primary target Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf
  (572 MB) fits the 2 GiB window directly, no slicing needed. U10/U11
  stay documented as the 27B stretch-goal track, unblocked but optional.

Verified facts this design stands on (probed 2026-07-15)
- HTIF window file I/O works on QEMU + all 3 vsim engines, 26 MB/s,
  1984 B/chunk; `_gettimeofday` works.
- C++ exceptions/ctors work bare-metal; printf INSIDE the ROI works on
  the vsim leg; a 3.6 MB image crossing the DLM window (0x200000)
  survives the handoff bit-exact.
- Hybrid QEMU leg is engine-synced (`-cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512`), no
  zfh/zvfh; RTL is ELEN=32. llama.cpp must be built with
  `GGML_RV_ZFH=OFF GGML_RV_ZVFH=OFF GGML_CPU_REPACK=OFF -mext-zvlsseg`.
- Standalone fast mode pins `-cpu andes-ax46mpv` (Zce, no Zcd): FP code
  from the default multilib traps there. vlinux runs are engine-synced
  or must pass `-- -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512` until U2 fixes the
  default for `--runtime linux`.
- Bonsai-4B-Q1_0.gguf is architecture `qwen3` (2560 embed, 36 layers,
  32 heads, 32768 ctx, 398 tensors) - a standard llama.cpp arch, no
  custom model code needed. Confirmed end-to-end OUTSIDE andesim
  (2026-07-15): `/home/nick/work/llama.cpp/run-rv64-qemu.sh` runs the
  cross-compiled `llama-completion` under Andes's linux-user QEMU
  (`qemu-riscv64`, syscall translation, no system emulation - a
  functional-only sanity check, unrelated to andesim's hybrid pipeline)
  and it generates correct text at `-t 1` ("The capital of France is
  Paris."), proving the model loads and every ggml op it needs already
  runs on RVV. That build (`build-rv64/`, `build-rv64-noomp/`) is
  **dynamic** (`BUILD_SHARED_LIBS=ON`) with `GGML_RV_ZFH/ZVFH/CPU_REPACK=ON`
  - the opposite link mode and feature set vlinux needs (static,
  those three OFF per the line above), so U8 still needs its own build;
  this only de-risks the syscall/threading/model-format assumptions.
- `build-rv64-baremetal/` (a prior newlib-baremetal attempt via
  `cmake/riscv64-andes-elf-newlib-gcc.cmake`) is abandoned: the
  toolchain file no longer exists and it produced zero binaries. Not a
  usable shortcut around vlinux; ignore that directory.

## Guest memory map (vlinux contract, DRAM base 0x0)

| Region                  | Range                          | Owner |
|-------------------------|--------------------------------|-------|
| ILM aperture            | 0x0000_0000 .. 0x0000_FFFF     | platform (apps link at >= 0x10000, no overlap) |
| App image (PT_LOADs)    | link base (0x10000/0x50000) .. | app ELF; loader rejects overlap with vlinux |
| brk arena               | app image end .. 0x0200_0000   | `brk` grows up; when full glibc malloc falls back to mmap |
| vlinux                  | 0x0200_0000 .. 0x0220_0000     | proxy text/data/bss + its own stack (2 MB) |
| mmap arena              | 0x0220_0000 .. initial stack   | grows DOWN from just below the app stack |
| App initial stack       | top 8 MB below `mem_size`      | built by loader (argc/argv/envp/auxv) |
| V-scratch               | `mem_size` .. +4 KB            | hybrid V transport (existing, untouched) |

DLM aperture 0x200000..0x207fff sits inside the app-image range; content
across it is transported by the existing LM sidecars (probe-verified).
Every arena bound is checked: exhaustion returns -ENOMEM / fails loudly
(no silent vplat-style `_sbrk` corruption).

---

## U0. Extract shared HTIF window client (structural)

- Description: move the window protocol client (`win_syscall`, slot
  staging, chunk loop) and `uart_putc` out of `runtime/vplat_syscalls.c`
  into `runtime/htif_client.{c,h}` so vplat and vlinux share one
  implementation. No behavior change.
- Input/Output: existing vplat fixtures before == after.
- Key files: runtime/htif_client.c (new), runtime/htif_client.h (new),
  runtime/vplat_syscalls.c, runtime/Makefile
- Test: existing tests/vplat/*.sh all stay green (that IS the test).
- Depends on: nothing
- State: DONE (2026-07-15) - htif_uart_putc/htif_syscall/htif_win_*/
  htif_call_str*/htif_write/htif_read now live in runtime/htif_client.{c,h};
  vplat_syscalls.c is a thin newlib adapter over them. All 12
  tests/vplat/*.sh green before and after (byte-identical output).

## U1. vlinux skeleton: boot, banner, manifest reader

- Description: new `runtime/linux/` payload with its own crt.S + linker
  script at 0x0200_0000 (built with HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN, freestanding +
  newlib for internal printf). Boots via `-bios vlinux.elf` on fast and
  cycle, enables caches/FS/VS/UNA (the crt0 duties, so the existing
  mcache_ctl/write-mask transport keeps working), prints a banner, reads
  the `.manifest` section (magic+version, mem_size, app path, argv,
  envp; "empty manifest" default = banner + exit 0), exits via
  SimControl.
- Input/Output: `vlinux.elf` with default manifest -> stdout contains
  `vlinux: boot ok mem=<N>M` and exit code 0 on BOTH fast and cycle.
- Key files: runtime/linux/{crt.S,vlinux.ld,main.c,manifest.h},
  runtime/linux/Makefile, scripts/build_all.sh
- Test: tests/vlinux/test_vlinux_boot.sh (fast leg + sim_ax45mpv_premium)
- Depends on: U0
- State: DONE (2026-07-15) - runtime/linux/{manifest.h,main.c,vlinux.ld,
  Makefile} + tests/vlinux/test_vlinux_boot.sh + scripts/build_all.sh
  `vlinux` target. No new crt.S: ../crt0.S (shared with vplat) enables
  icache/dcache/mstatus.FS+VS/mmisc_ctl.UNA using only PC-relative
  addressing and a linker-provided `_stack` symbol, so it is already
  link-address-agnostic and vlinux.ld's `PROVIDE(_stack = 0x02200000)` +
  `. = 0x02000000` base retarget it with zero new code (CLAUDE.md: don't
  duplicate code). vlinux.elf links main.c straight against
  build/runtime/{crt0.o,libandesim_runtime.a} (no -specs=andesim.specs -
  vlinux is a kernel image, not a user program built with the two-flag
  command). Confirmed via research (QEMU andes_ae350.c +
  riscv_setup_rom_reset_vec, and the external vsim's load_elf) that
  `-bios` on both engines boots from the ELF's own e_entry with no reset
  stub needed at any fixed low address - 0x0200_0000 "just works". Test
  runs vlinux.elf as a plain standalone ELF (no --runtime flag yet -
  that's U2): `./andesim run --mode fast` + `sim_ax45mpv_premium` direct,
  same pattern as tests/vplat/test_vplat_f1.sh + f2.sh. All 12
  tests/vplat/*.sh + the build_all.sh/release_surface driver contract
  tests stay green.

## U2. Driver: `--runtime linux` plumbing

- Description: new run flag. The driver copies vlinux.elf per run and
  `objcopy --update-section .manifest=<blob>` (toolchain objcopy from
  config.env) with: absolute app ELF path, `mem_size`, argv[0..n] (from
  `-- <args...>`, now ALLOWED in hybrid for the linux runtime - they are
  app argv, not engine argv), minimal envp. The manifested vlinux.elf is
  what every leg loads, so fast/cycle/hybrid stay uniform. Linux runtime
  defaults: `--mem-size 1G`; standalone fast leg uses the engine-synced
  CPU (`andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512`), not the ax46 default. `--pc-start/end`
  symbols resolve against the APP ELF in this mode.
- Input/Output: `./andesim run --mode fast --runtime linux app.elf -- -m x.gguf -t 1`
  -> dry-run prints the objcopy step + `-bios <workdir>/vlinux-run.elf`;
  manifest blob round-trips (dump tool or readelf grep).
- Key files: driver/cli.cpp, driver/cmd_run.cpp, driver/run_plan.cpp,
  driver/manifest.cpp (new), docs/USER_GUIDE.md
- Test: tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_runtime_linux.sh (dry-run
  contract + manifest content grep)
- Depends on: U1
- State: DONE (2026-07-15) - driver/{manifest.hpp,manifest.cpp,tempdir.hpp,
  tempdir.cpp} (new) + `--runtime` on Cli (cli.hpp/cli.cpp) +
  run_fast/run_standalone wiring in cmd_run.cpp +
  tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_runtime_linux.sh + docs/USER_GUIDE.md 5.12.
  Three deliberate scope cuts from the paragraph above, each documented at
  its call site:
  1. **`--mode fast` only.** `driver/run_plan.cpp` (hybrid's multi-leg
     executor) turned out NOT to need touching: cycle/hybrid go through a
     different code path than fast/cycle's `run_standalone`, and the
     roadmap's own Order line (U0->...->U8 all run on the fast leg; hybrid
     wiring is explicitly U9) means nothing downstream needs cycle/hybrid
     support yet. `cmd_run()` REJECTS `--runtime` with anything but
     `--mode fast` (a clear error naming U9), rather than silently
     ignoring it -- an untested silent accept would be worse than a loud
     not-yet-supported.
  2. **argv/envp deferred to U3.** `runtime/linux/manifest.h`'s own U1-era

     version once U3 needs them." Building a wire format for them now, with
     no consumer (vlinux's loader, U3) to validate the design against, is
     exactly the untested-speculative-format risk TDD guards against -- a
     wrong guess would just be redone at U3. `-- <args...>` still PARSES

     and drops it rather than forwarding it into QEMU's own CLI, where it
     would be misparsed as engine flags (`-m x.gguf` is not a memory size).

     a dry run (its qemu.cfg is disposable/re-derivable), whereas
     vlinux-run.elf is the actual `-bios` target if `--dry-run` is dropped
     and the run repeats for real, and the U2 contract itself
     ("manifest blob round-trips... readelf grep") only works if the file
     is still on disk after the command returns. Net effect: both dry-run
     and a real run leave one small workdir under the system temp dir per

- Description: vlinux HTIF-reads the app ELF (26 MB/s -> ~0.5 s for a
  10 MB binary), maps PT_LOADs (reject overlap with vlinux/V-scratch/

  app arena: argc/argv/envp then auxv (AT_PHDR/PHENT/PHNUM from the
  loaded headers, AT_ENTRY, AT_PAGESZ=4096, AT_RANDOM 16 bytes,
  AT_HWCAP=IMAFDCV bits, AT_UID/GID/EUID/EGID=0, AT_SECURE=0,
  AT_EXECFN), sets sp, jumps to the app entry in M-mode.
- Input/Output: a -nostdlib linux-ABI asm/C fixture (reads argc/argv
  from sp, calls raw `write(1,...)` + `exit_group`) prints its argv and

- Key files: runtime/linux/{loader.c,stack.c}, tests/fixtures Makefile
  (new LINUX_TOOLCHAIN fixtures; config.env.example gains
  LINUX_TOOLCHAIN=/local/nick/SW_Release/build-ast542/build-toolchain/linux/nds64le-linux-glibc-v5d)
- Test: tests/vlinux/test_vlinux_loader.sh (fast + cycle, argv echo)
- Depends on: U1, U2
- State: DONE (2026-07-15) - runtime/linux/{loader.h,loader.c,stack.h,
  stack.c,syscall.c} (new) + runtime/ecall_hook.h (new, shared) +
  runtime/handler.c (extended) + runtime/linux/{main.c,Makefile,vlinux.ld}

  1. **No LINUX_TOOLCHAIN dependency yet.** The roadmap's own fixture is

     risks getting redone anyway.

     a duplicated magic address) but not yet the V-scratch page or the HTIF
     window MMIO range, since standalone fast/cycle (the only wired modes)
     never reserve V-scratch at all - that only matters once U9 wires
     `--runtime linux` under hybrid.
  4. **`_sbrk`'s brk arena is not app-arena-aware.** vplat_syscalls.c's
     `_sbrk` still grows from vlinux's OWN `_end`, not the app's. Harmless
     today (the U3 fixture never calls malloc/brk) but a real gap for U4+,
     when a glibc app's malloc will need the app's own brk arena
     (roadmap: "app image end .. 0x0200_0000"), not vlinux's leftover space.

  1. **`const` on `g_manifest` silently broke the loader.** U1 declared
     `g_manifest` plain `const` for section placement; at -O1 GCC constant-
     folded every read back to the empty-string initializer, since nothing
     in the visible program ever writes it - U2's post-link `objcopy
     --update-section` patch is invisible to the compiler. vlinux booted
     the "empty manifest" banner path even with a fully-correct staged
     app_path on disk. Fixed with `const volatile` (never written by this
     program, but its value changes through means outside the compiler's
     view) + a one-time snapshot into plain locals in `main()` so
     loader.c/stack.c see ordinary unqualified types.
  2. **Missing `fence.i` before jumping to freshly-loaded code.** The app's
     code is written via ordinary guest stores (through the D-cache crt0.S
     enables), not vsim's privileged ELF-load backdoor. Fast (QEMU, no cache
     model) worked first try; cycle (the real RTL) faulted with an illegal
     instruction reading back all-zero at the app's entry point - a classic
     self-modifying-code hazard, not an address or memory-map bug (verified
     by relinking the fixture to 0x00100000, andesim.ld's own proven base,
     which failed identically; reverted once `fence.i` - added in
     `enter_app()` right before the jump - fixed it at the roadmap's
     original 0x10000). Required by the RISC-V spec whenever a hart writes
     then executes new code; QEMU's cachelessness had been masking that this
     was ever missing.

  rdcycle-seeded), sched_getaffinity(123; 1-cpu mask), sched_yield(124),
  rt_sigaction(134)/rt_sigprocmask(135)/sigaltstack(132) -> record+0
  (no delivery exists), tgkill(131) on fatal signal -> SimControl exit
  128+sig, ioctl(29 -ENOTTY), fcntl(25 basic). Unknown syscall -> print
  `vlinux: ENOSYS <nr>` once + return -ENOSYS (loud, grep-able).
- Input/Output: glibc-static fixture using argv + malloc(1MB) + printf +
  fflush + exit(42) -> exact stdout + exit code 42, fast AND cycle.
- Key files: runtime/linux/{trap.S,syscall.c,mm.c}
- Test: tests/vlinux/test_vlinux_glibc_hello.sh
- Risk to check here: Andes vendor glibc may use riscv_hwprobe(258) for
  str* ifuncs at startup -> implement as -ENOSYS first (glibc falls back
  to generic); if the vendor libc hard-requires it, answer the base
  key set instead.
- Depends on: U3
- State: DONE, WITH ONE DOCUMENTED GAP (2026-07-15) -

  static/global variable) ran with WHATEVER gp was active at the moment

  the app is running. Silent in U3 (syscall.c had zero global variables,
  so nothing was gp-relative yet); U4's `mm.c` globals (`g_brk_cur` etc.)

  vlinux's own correct gp) set them correctly, but `sys_brk()` (running
  later, from the trap handler, with the APP's gp) computed a completely
  different address for "the same" variable and read back zero every
  time. Fixed with the same `.option norelax` / `lla gp,
  __global_pointer$` sequence crt0.S already uses at boot, inserted into

  trap that already shares one image with its handler (every existing
  vplat fixture, and U3's own fixture, which is why this was never
  visible before).

  A second, separate real bug (arena-boundary arithmetic, not gp-related):
  **the mmap arena's start point overlapped the app's own live stack.**
  `stack.c`'s initial-stack builder started writing AT `mem_size -
  STACK_RESERVE` -- meant to be the stack's FLOOR (the boundary
  `mm.c`'s mmap arena must not cross) -- instead of at `mem_size` (the
  true top, with the reserved 8 MiB as growth headroom below it). The
  build's own content therefore immediately spilled below the floor, and
  the very first substantial `mmap()` call (malloc's 1 MiB request)
  landed exactly on top of the app's own already-in-use stack and
  zeroed it (mmap returns zeroed pages), corrupting a saved return
  address a few calls later. Fixed by starting the build at `mem_size`
  instead. Caught because the crash was a "return to a garbage stack
  address" pattern immediately downstream of the first big `mmap` call,
  not an obvious out-of-bounds fault -- the value that got zeroed was a
  legitimate stack slot the app hadn't returned through yet.

  LINUX_TOOLCHAIN's own sysroot headers rather than assumed (asm-generic/

     bit layout instead (only the low 2 access-mode bits agree -- O_CREAT

     not a workaround. Missing this would silently drop O_CREAT

     the untranslated case) and `fopen(path, "w")` would fail ENOENT.

     byte offsets in whatever buffer address they are given -- st_mode

     (`andes_ae350.c andesim_store_guest_stat`, matching vsim's mirror).

     (which is what the existing vplat client relies on), but Linux's
     riscv64 `struct stat` puts st_mode at +16 and st_size at +48 --
     completely different layout. `fill_stat_from_host()`/`sys_statx()`
     read the host's two fields into a small scratch buffer, then
     construct a real Linux-shaped `struct stat`/`struct statx` at the
     correct offsets (zeroing everything not known; `statx`'s `stx_mask`
     correctly reports only the fields actually filled, per the statx(2)
     contract -- not a shortcut). Also verified: `faccessat` (syscall 48)
     takes exactly 3 arguments at the raw-syscall ABI level (dirfd, path,
     mode) -- no flags, unlike the `faccessat()` library wrapper, which
     implements `AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW`/`AT_EACCESS` itself in userspace --
     so the 4th register is never forwarded as flags (would be garbage).

     real `getcwd(2)` syscall's "bytes written including NUL" return by
     measuring the string vlinux just read back.

  content in vlinux.elf, vsim's own positional arg). QEMU's plugin has no
  such limitation (it watches the executed instruction stream, content-
  agnostic). Fixed entirely driver-side, per the roadmap's explicit
  no-vsim-source-changes constraint: `driver/elf_syms.{hpp,cpp}` gained
  `find_roi_markers()` (mirrors `CsrTrigger::scan_buffer`'s exact RVC-aware
  scan, via the ALREADY-SHARED `include/hybrid/insn_match.h` so there is
  no reimplementation drift), and `cmd_run.cpp`'s `run_hybrid()` uses it to
  resolve the app ELF's own exit marker to a PC, then converts vsim's leg
  from marker-trigger to `--trigger pc`'s existing `--hybrid-exit-pc` flag
  - an EXISTING vsim CLI flag, reused not added. QEMU's leg stays
  marker-triggered (its plugin has no gap to work around). Zero vsim
  source changes, as required.

  **`--step-timeout-ms` (new CLI flag, a real gap this feature exposed):**
  `PlanOptions.timeout_ms` (`driver/run_plan.hpp`) was hardcoded to 90000
  with no override - fine for every fixture-scale ROI to date, but a real
  transformer matmul on the ~8.6 kHz cycle-accurate leg legitimately needs
  minutes, not seconds. Added `--step-timeout-ms <ms>` (`cli.hpp`/`cli.cpp`
  table-driven parser, same pattern as `--mem-size`), threaded into
  `PlanOptions.timeout_ms` in `cmd_run.cpp` with the same string-parse-and-
  `fail()` convention as the existing numeric flags. RED test
  (`driver/cli_test.cpp`) written first (compile failure: `Cli` has no
  `step_timeout_ms` member) before adding the field: TDD gate satisfied
  for the parsing layer; the end-to-end plumbing is covered by
  `tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_step_timeout.sh` (new: default-timeout
  baseline, an absurd 1ms timeout failing with the right message, a
  generous explicit timeout still succeeding, and a non-positive-integer
  value rejected cleanly).

  **The real llama-completion run: four distinct genuine illegal-
  instruction sites, all the SAME root-cause FAMILY as U3/U4/U5's
  "fast-permissive/cycle-enforces" pattern, now at the ELEN/vector-unit
  level instead of the memory/CSR level** - QEMU's hybrid-leg CPU model is
  engine-synced (`elen=32` from the accurate `-readconfig`, unlike fast
  mode's own hardcoded, unconstrained `-cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512`
  string), so QEMU1 itself now enforces the real ELEN=32/vector-FPU limit
  that fast mode's own cpu string never did - every one of these four was
  first caught as an illegal-instruction trap (mcause=2) on QEMU1, not
  vsim, confirmed via manual `mepc`/`mtval` disassembly at the exact fault
  PC each time:
  1. **`ggml_vec_dot_f16`/`ggml_vec_dot_bf16`** (`ggml/src/ggml-cpu/vec.cpp`,
     llama.cpp repo): each has a `ggml_float` (double) scalar-accumulated
     fallback loop, taken because this build has neither `__riscv_zvfh`
     nor `__riscv_zvfbfwma` - GCC's auto-vectorizer lowers that plain
     scalar reduction into a widening e64 vector reduce anyway. Fixed with
     `__attribute__((target("arch=rv64gc")))` on just these two functions
     (confirmed empirically that GCC's RISC-V port honors this - unlike
     the `optimize` function attribute and `#pragma GCC push_options`,
     both tried and confirmed NOT to suppress the vectorization, objdump-
     verified either way): forces scalar codegen for exactly the fallback
     path, leaving the real (unreached, in this build) RVV intrinsic path
     above it untouched.
  2. **`ggml_vec_cvar_f32`/`ggml_vec_soft_max_f32`** (same file): unlike
     site 1, these use EXPLICIT, unconditional RVV intrinsics - a
     `vfloat64m1_t` accumulator via `vfwredusum_vs_f32m2_f64m1` (widening
     reduce, f32 lanes to an f64 total). Every OTHER architecture's branch
     in the same two functions (AVX512/AVX2/SSE2/NEON) does the opposite:
     reduce in NATIVE precision (f32) with a plain SIMD op, then widen
     ONE scalar partial-sum per chunk to `ggml_float` in ordinary C. The
     RISC-V branch was the sole outlier, and the ONLY reason it needs e64
     at all - a real algorithmic inconsistency versus its own siblings in
     the same file, not a hardware requirement to route around. Fixed by
     rewriting both to match: `vfredusum_vs_f32m2_f32m1` (non-widening)
     inside the loop, `sum += (ggml_float) partial` in scalar C - zero e64,
     same numerics as every non-RISC-V build already computes.
  3. **`quantize_row_q8_0`/`quantize_row_q8_1`** (`ggml/src/ggml-cpu/
     arch/riscv/quants.c`): hardcoded `vfloat32m8_t`/LMUL=8 for
     `__riscv_vfabs_v_f32m8`+`vfredmax`, unconditionally (no smaller-LMUL
     variant, unlike the vl1024/vl512/vl256/vl128-suffixed dispatch every
     OTHER quant kernel in this file has). `ax45mpv_premium`'s vector FPU
     datapath does not extend to LMUL=8 for floating-point ops (`mtval`
     decoded to exactly this `vfabs.v` instruction's own encoding;
     correlates with the engine's `isa-vl4` config bit in the accurately-
     synced `qemu.cfg`, though QEMU itself does not enforce it - only
     vsim's RTL does, hence this one surfaced on vsim, not QEMU1, unlike
     sites 1/2/4). Confirmed the INTEGER path (a plain `vle32.v` load at
     the same LMUL=8) executes fine immediately before the FP op faults -
     the datapath limit is FP-specific, not a blanket LMUL cap. Per
     TDD.md's "remove and rewrite, don't patch": both functions' bodies
     now call their existing, portable `_ref` scalar implementations
     unconditionally (`ggml-quants.c`, already used as the non-RVV
     fallback everywhere else) - a real, minimal source change, not a
     build-flag suppression (the vector branch here is the ONLY
     implementation, unlike site 1, so no compiler flag can select an
     already-existing alternative). This is activation quantization,
     called once per token row before the (still fully vectorized,
     unaffected) `ggml_vec_dot_q1_0_q8_0` dot-product loop reuses it - a
     trivial fraction of total matmul cost, confirmed by the fact that the
     eventual successful run's cycle count matches the dot-product-loop-
     dominated estimate, not a quantization-dominated one.
  4. **A stale ccache / incomplete incremental rebuild, not a code bug**:
     after fixing site 3 in `ggml-cpu.c`'s neighborhood, a rebuild's
     `compile_commands.json` showed the correct constrained `-march` for
     `ggml-cpu.c.o` yet the crash (this time inside `ggml_table_f32_f16`'s
     region - later found to actually be `ggml_vec_dot_f16`, site 1,
     misattributed at the time from a stale disassembly) persisted
     identically. A `find -delete` + rebuild did not reproduce the object
     file at all in the build log; only an explicit `rm -f` of the exact
     `.o` path followed by a fresh build actually recompiled it. Recorded
     here as a standalone gotcha since it cost real debugging time before
     being recognized as a build-cache artifact rather than a fix that
     "didn't work."

  **The cycle-accurate leg's own diagnostic gap, found and fixed while
  root-causing site 3 (which only manifests on vsim, not QEMU1):**
  `runtime/handler.c`'s `exception_handler` (shared by vplat AND vlinux,
  every trap on every engine) calls `fprintf(stderr, ...)` then
  `_exit((int) mcause)` - `_exit()` (unlike `exit()`) never flushes stdio,
  so on any path where stderr is not unbuffered (confirmed: the vlinux
  syscall-backed stdio path is fully buffered, unlike whatever made this
  visible on QEMU1's crashes earlier in this same investigation) the
  entire diagnostic is silently lost, every time, on every future vlinux
  trap - not specific to this session's debugging. Fixed with an
  `fflush(stderr)` before `_exit()` (a real, permanent correctness fix,
  not a debugging aid). A second, deliberately-kept addition: a
  `raw_print_hex()` helper that writes `mcause`/`mepc`/`mtval` straight to
  the UART MMIO register via the existing `htif_uart_putc()` (no stdio,
  no malloc, no buffering) BEFORE attempting the `fprintf` path - cheap
  insurance for the next trap whose corrupted state might take out
  `fprintf`/`vfprintf` themselves. (Separately, and not fixed here since
  it is orthogonal to the guest-side bug: the `andesim` driver's own
  capture of a subprocess's stdout was observed to silently drop vsim's
  raw output in at least one investigation path; invoking `sim_ax45mpv_premium`
  directly, bypassing the driver, is what actually surfaced the guest's
  UART bytes. Worth a future driver-side look if it recurs.)

  **ROI target selection - the roadmap's own "confirm actual figure once
  measured" note, taken literally.** The roadmap's initial pick (K=50, per
  earlier gdb-based node counting: 253 mul_mat calls per token, 36 layers
  x 7 matmuls + 1 lm_head; K=50 lands on layer 7's Q projection,
  2560->4096) is real, correctly-executing, e64-free code by the time
  sites 1-4 were fixed - but too large a computation for the ~8.6 kHz
  cycle-accurate leg to finish inside even a 900000ms (15 min)
  `--step-timeout-ms` budget. Rather than keep raising the timeout
  blindly, dumped every mul_mat call's operand shapes for one real forward
  pass on a NATIVE x86 build (`build-host/`, a throwaway
  `ANDESIM_DUMP_MUL_MAT_SIZES`-gated `fprintf` in `ggml-cpu.c`, reverted
  after use - fast, no simulation needed) to rank relative cost:
  Q/O-projection and FFN gate/up/down are all 2560x4096..2560x9728 (the
  FFN matmuls are ~2.4x LARGER than Q, not smaller); K/V-projection
  (2560x1024, grouped-query attention's narrower KV head count) is the
  smallest matmul shape anywhere in this architecture, ~4x fewer MACs than
  Q. Retargeted to K=51 (layer 7's V projection, the very next node after
  the original pick) - `ANDESIM_ROI_MUL_MAT_K` is a build-time `-D`, no
  source change, just a `cmake -B build-rv64-static` reconfigure. Verified
  the resulting binary actually recompiled with the new value via
  `compile_commands.json` (not just trusted the reconfigure, per the site-4
  gotcha above). Completed comfortably inside the 900000ms budget both
  times: **6528953 cycles**.

  Full regression (14 driver C++ unit tests including the new
  `--step-timeout-ms` cases, 44 tests/andes_sim + tests/vplat scripts
  including the new `test_andes_sim_step_timeout.sh`, all 7
  tests/vlinux/*.sh including `test_vlinux_hybrid_roi.sh`) stayed green
  throughout; the real llama-completion hybrid run itself is manual-tier
  like every other U8+ llama fixture, run to completion twice this session
  with an identical cycle count both times.

## U10. Platform track: DRAM window >= 6 GB (full Bonsai-27B) [stretch, off critical path]

- Description: lift the 2 GiB ceiling so the untouched 3.8 GB GGUF +
  arenas (~4.5 GB) fit. Three coordinated changes: (1) qemu_andesim
  andes_ae350 machine model DRAM window (currently "Cannot model more

- Input/Output: `--mem-size 6G` accepted; U8 smoke passes with the full

- Key files: qemu_andesim (hw/riscv/andes_ae350.c), hybrid_vsim repo,

- Depends on: independent of U0-U9 (parallel track). NOT needed for the

Findings: 2 real issues, 3 areas checked clean.

**1. driver/cmd_run.cpp:612-624 (--step-timeout-ms parsing) - duplicates existing code**
This 13-line try/catch reimplements `parse_knob()` (driver/cmd_profile.cpp:214-226) almost line for line: same empty-check, same `stoi`+pos-check, same positivity check, same catch-all. `parse_knob` sits in an anonymous namespace so cmd_run.cpp cannot call it directly, but `driver/strutil.hpp` already exists as the shared home for exactly this kind of helper (currently holds `ljust`/`join`/`vlen_str`).

Simpler form: move a `parse_positive_int(v, def, out)` into strutil.hpp, used by both files:
```
int ms = 90000;
if (!parse_positive_int(cli.step_timeout_ms, 90000, ms))
  return fail("--step-timeout-ms: not a positive integer: " + cli.step_timeout_ms);
opts.timeout_ms = ms;
```
Also note: `parse_size` (shm.cpp:56, used for `--mem-size`) needs no manual "consumed == size" check and no try/catch at all - `std::regex_match` anchors the whole string, and it returns 0 + sets `err` instead of throwing. That is the simpler baseline shape this new flag should have followed.

**2. docs/llama_roi_howto.md:194-196 (section 5 repro command) - references a nonexistent CMake option**
`-UGGML_RV_ZVE32F` does not exist anywhere in this llama.cpp checkout (`ggml/CMakeLists.txt` defines `GGML_RV_ZFH`, `GGML_RV_ZVFH`, `GGML_RV_ZICBOP`, `GGML_RV_ZIHINTPAUSE`, `GGML_RV_ZVFBFWMA`, `GGML_RVV` - no ZVE32F, verified by grep). The command also omits `-DGGML_RV_ZFH=OFF -DGGML_RV_ZVFH=OFF -DGGML_CPU_REPACK=OFF`, which `ROADMAP_LINUX_RUNTIME.md`'s own U8 section says this exact build requires; all three default ON. Run verbatim on a fresh build dir, this silently builds with zfh/zvfh/repack all ON, contradicting the doc's own "Confirmed end to end" claim.

Fix: replace `-UGGML_RV_ZVE32F` with the three real `-D...=OFF` flags already documented in the roadmap.

**Checked, no issue:**
- `runtime/handler.c` raw_print_hex + WRITE_ERROR: not redundant. raw_print_hex is raw UART MMIO (bypasses stdio entirely, only 3 fields); WRITE_ERROR is the fprintf path with strictly more fields (mdcause, ra, a0) and runs regardless. Comment and both docs justify it as insurance against fprintf itself being broken mid-fault. Justified dual path.
- `ggml-cpu/vec.cpp` ggml_vec_cvar_f32/soft_max_f32: per-iteration zero-vector construction mirrors every sibling AVX2/SSE2/NEON branch's own style (all recompute broadcast operands per-chunk too) - consistent, not new complexity.
- `arch/riscv/quants.c`: `nb` and its `GGML_UNUSED` guard fully removed, no dead code or orphaned includes (file's other functions still use RVV intrinsics).
